meta.title: Cluster Cutover Briefing
meta.subject: Saturday 02:00 window — Hub BFF route flip to CRS spec-ack
meta.author: LIS Team

slides.headline:
Cluster Cutover
Saturday 02:00
slides.lede: Flip the Hub BFF route onto the new CRS specimen-acknowledgement service during the first quiet window this month. No schema change. Rollback is the previous Helm revision.
slides.footer: Draft — from the 12 Aug cutover huddle
slides.notes: This is an operations briefing, not a design review. The decision is already made; tonight is execution. Quiet window starts at 02:00 because Friday outpatient phlebotomy runs until midnight.

slides.title: How we got to Saturday 02:00

steps.title: Daytime is too hot
steps.body: A08 traffic and ward collections overlap until evening. A daytime flip would strand acknowledgements in flight.

steps.title: Friday is still live
steps.body: Outpatient phlebotomy runs until midnight. Queue depth falls only after the last batch.

steps.title: First quiet window
steps.body: One-hour window. Rollback is the previous Helm revision, kept for 72 hours.

callout.text: Wait for the queue to drain. Do not pause clinical traffic to make the window.

slides.notes: Friday night still has outpatient traffic until midnight. Saturday 02:00 is the first quiet window this month. If the queue has not drained by 02:20 we slip a week rather than cutting hot.

slides.title: What changes tonight

cards.title: Hub BFF flips
cards.body: The shell points acknowledgements at the new CRS spec-ack service. Callers do not change.

cards.title: Dictionary warms
cards.body: Warm the keyword and location cache for fifteen minutes before the flip so the first ack is not cold.

cards.title: Nothing in the database
cards.body: No schema change, no PMI backfill, no setup-data load. If we roll back, we only roll the route.

callout.text: If anything else is in the release train, it does not ride this window.

slides.notes: The only moving part is the BFF route plus a cache warm. Saying 'no DDL' out loud stops the 'did we migrate' question in the room.

slides.title: Three steps, then watch

steps.title: Drain inbound A08
steps.body: Watch queue depth until flat. Do not flip while acks are landing.

steps.title: Flip the BFF route
steps.body: Helm revision on the BFF only. Confirm the spec-ack target in the live config.

steps.title: Verify the first ack
steps.body: One real acknowledgement from a quiet ward, then watch error rate for 20 minutes.

sidebar.headline: Slip a week
sidebar.body: If the queue is still moving at 02:20, we do not cut. Next window is Saturday.

slides.notes: Drain, flip, verify. The abort is a date, not a heroics clause — 02:20 and we are done for the night.

slides.title: We cut only if every row is green

takeaways.title: All four Go, then flip
takeaways.body: The matrix is the go-live checklist. Do not add a fifth check.

takeaways.title: Any No-go slips a week
takeaways.body: Do not negotiate a weaker row at 02:00. The next window is already held.

slides.notes: Read the matrix top to bottom before the flip, not after. Queue depth is the one that usually fails — that is why drain is step one.

slides.headline: Window opens
slides.note: 02:00–03:00. If we abort, the next Saturday is already held.

nextSteps.title: Pin the previous Helm revision
nextSteps.body: Before the window, not during it. Rollback is a one-line roll, not a hunt.

nextSteps.title: On-call on the bridge at 01:45
nextSteps.body: Queue watch starts fifteen minutes early so 02:00 is a decision, not a surprise.

nextSteps.title: Write the outcome by 09:00
nextSteps.body: Cut or slipped, with the matrix row that decided it. Duty AM owns the note.

slides.notes: Leave with three owners: pin the revision, be on the bridge at 01:45, write the outcome in the morning. The date on the slide is the window, not a target completion for a change request.
